title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §13 of the notes on the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}, 'Digressions sur stratifications locales en général'. It is the topological groundwork for describing the Deligne–Mumford boundary. Its strata, indexed by dual graphs, are not embedded in a 'unibranch' way: the boundary divisor Δ_0 self-intersects. The next page introduces D*_{Δ0} → X as a bijective local immersion.

The page finishes axiom (e) of a 'global stratification' of a space X. Recall the earlier axioms: (a) the strata are locally closed and the family is locally finite; (b) the strata are manifolds; (c) the strata are locally connected, and closures meet other strata in unions of components; (d) the local germ of each stratum at any point of its closure is connected.

Axiom (e) is a local product condition. Near X_i, the configuration of closures \bar X_j ⊇ X_i is isomorphic to X_i × Z, where Z is a normal slice:
- each X_j corresponds to Z_j ⊂ Z, and \bar X_j to \bar Z_j;
- X_i corresponds to a point z_0 lying in all the \bar Z_j;
- the 'local π_0' π_0(Z_j; \bar Z_j, z_0) is a singleton, i.e. z_0 has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods V with V ∩ Z_j connected.
So the condition is topological local triviality along strata (Thom–Mather style) plus a unibranch condition: each bigger stratum is locally unibranch along each smaller one. A marginal note adds that the Z_j are locally connected.

Remarks:
1. For U open, the connected components of the U ∩ X_i form a global stratification of U.
2. Hence U ↦ Strat_glob(U) is a presheaf on X.
3. The examples of (d) show it is not a sheaf. These are the nodal curve, and a disc with a boundary point treated as a stratum. Foliations give another non-sheaf example.
4. Sections of the associated sheaf are called 'structures de stratifications locales'. They are compared with the SGA (topos theory) notion of local equivalence relations, of which stratifications are 'very particular examples' (the sentence continues on the next page).

The point is that a locally given stratification can be glued even when strata self-intersect or are not unibranch. Globally one then gets a partition into strata, each carrying its own finer topology, with the inclusion a bijective local immersion, as for the leaves of a foliation. This is exactly what is needed for strata such as Δ_0 of \bar M_{g,ν}, whose 'global strata' must be taken as normalisation-like immersed objects.

A marginal remark muses that a global (pre)stratification is like a stronger condition compared with a locally defined one.
errors: No real error. One wording issue: π_0(Z_j; \bar Z_j, z_0) presupposes z_0 ∈ \bar Z_j, which is stated, and is meant as the pro-set of local components (local π_0). The equivalence with 'cardinal 1 iff some fundamental system of neighbourhoods meets Z_j connectedly' is correct as an informal reading.
Restriction to U preserves (a)–(e) because all conditions are local or componentwise, so the presheaf claim is fine.
The claim that the sheafification yields partitions into strata with finer topology and bijective local immersions is only asserted (and continued on the next page), not proved.

ideas.what: Global stratification with local product structure along strata via a normal slice Z, plus a unibranch condition of bigger strata along smaller ones
ideas.modern_name: Topologically locally trivial (Thom–Mather / Whitney-type) stratification with locally connected (unibranch) strata; conical stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (1960s–70s); Goresky–MacPherson; Siebenmann's locally cone-like spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§5, stratified structures / tame topology) discusses such stratifications informally; this precise axiom list is unsure

ideas.what: Presheaf U ↦ Strat_glob(U) is not a sheaf; its sheafification defines 'local stratification structures', whose strata are immersed (bijective local immersion from the disjoint union of strata, each with a finer topology)
ideas.modern_name: Locally defined stratifications with self-intersecting/non-unibranch strata, e.g. the stratification of a non-simple normal crossings divisor or of a log scheme by its log stratification; strata handled via normalisation, generalized cone complexes, Artin fans
ideas.usually_credited_to: Log geometry: K. Kato, Olsson; tropical/skeleton side: Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (2015), Abramovich–Chen–Marcus–Wise / Ulirsch for Artin fans

ideas.what: Analogy between local stratifications, foliations and local equivalence relations in topos theory (SGA 4)
ideas.modern_name: Foliation topoi / topos of a local equivalence relation; Haefliger's classifying topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: Haefliger, Moerdijk (foliation groupoids/topoi); local equivalence relations mentioned in SGA 4 context
ideas.where_published: Possibly exercises in SGA 4 on local equivalence relations (unsure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines 'local stratifications' as sections of the sheafification of the presheaf of global stratifications. Strata then become immersed objects with a finer topology. He develops this explicitly in order to treat the boundary of \bar M_{g,ν}, where Δ_0 self-intersects. This anticipates the device later used in tropical/log geometry: ACP generalized cone complexes and Artin fans, built because the boundary strata of \bar M_g are not unibranch. He also links it to foliations and local equivalence relations in topos theory, a link not usually drawn in that literature.
missed.quote: Les sections du faisceau associé s'appellent les structures de stratifications locales sur X. Comparer avec l'ancien de SGA (théorie des Topos) sur les relations d'équivalence locales
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a topos/groupoid-theoretic (foliation-like) formalism for self-intersecting stratifications, possibly unifying Artin fans, exit-path categories of non-unibranch stratifications and foliation topoi.

missed.claim: The axiomatics of local stratifications (sheaf-theoretic gluing of stratifications with a local-π_0 unibranch condition) is sketched but not completed. It is left as a digression, and the marginal note doubts whether the global notion is merely a stronger local condition.
missed.quote: j'ai l'impression cependant que une préstratification globale c'est comme une condition plus [forte?] que serait locale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean sheaf-theoretic definition of stratified spaces closed under gluing (strata as immersed manifolds) is still handled ad hoc in stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The local-product/unibranch axioms are standard. Defining local stratifications by sheafifying global ones, with strata as bijective local immersions like foliation leaves and an explicit link to topos-theoretic local equivalence relations, is a nice conceptual move motivated by \bar M_{g,ν}. It anticipates later log/tropical techniques, but is a sketch rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: 'forme une {+connexe [?]+} stratification globale de U' should read 'forme une stratification globale de U'.
The last line likely reads '— les stratifications en sont des exemples [très] particuliers' (continued by 'particulier.' on the next page), not 'les stratifications au sens des exemples ...'.
The margin probably reads 'j'ai l'impression cependant qu'une préstratification globale c'est comme une condition plus [forte] que serait locale'.
'l'ancien de SGA' may be 'l'ancien [exercice/rêve] de SGA'; the reading is uncertain.
The marginal 'NB les Z_j loc. connexes' is a gloss on condition (e).
